note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Nationality Act B.E.2508 (1965) 10(4), 11; A06b Nationality Act B.E.2508 (1965) 10, 12, 5; L05 THA 17(2), 19(2), 19(6)): ordinary naturalisation after 5 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Thailand, 2024
sources.said: An applicant has had a domicile in Thailand for a consecutive period of not less than five years until the date of filing the naturalisation application. This timeframe is not required for persons who: render distinguished service to Thailand, are the child, wife, or a naturalised or restored Thai citizen, used to have Thai nationality, are the husband of a Thai citizen. ... n.a. ... Person naturalises in another country (loss becomes effective upon publication in the gazette)
